units.tr: Book V of the Code.

units.la: HActenus de actionibus in personam ex contractu, ut dictum ad instit. titul. de obl. quae ex q. contract. sed actiones in personam oriuntur non tantum ex contractu vel quasi, ex delicto vel q. sed etiam ex aliis causis, ut ex aequo & bono ut qualis est actio de dote, quam Cujacius non recte ait esse ex contractu. Nam neque matrimonium est contractus, quia nullus contractus fit sine re. At matrimonium fieri potest sine re, hoc est sine dote, quia fit tantum personatum conjungendarum causa. Neque dos est contractus, quia est species donationis. l. ult. de donat. ante nupt. At donatio differt a contractu. l. Aristot. de donat. quare dotis actio non est ex contractu, sed ex aequo & bono, ut differte ait Caius l. 8. ea de cap. min. Explicatis autem ut dictum actionibus in personam ex contractu, non statim adjunguntur actiones ex q. contractu, sed interjicitur actio de dote, eamq; sequitur actio tutelae quae est ex q. contractu de quibus duobus de dote inquam, & tutela, agitur toto libro. Ratio ordinis, hoc est, cur actio de dote interjiciatur, sive praecedat actiones tutelae, exponetur infra ad ff. Quia autem actio de dote & tutela multis his titul. explicatur, ordinis melius intelligendi causa eas actiones sive titulos ad certa capita revocabimus. Ergo prior actio, quae est de dote f. capp. continetur, & titul. Nam primum caput est de sponsal. titul. 12. & 13. II. est de nuptiis, tit. 4. & 6. seqq. III. de dote, & ipsa actione dotis. titul. 11. & 12. int. seqq. IV. est de liberis. tit. vl. 24. & 5. tit. seqq. Idem fere est ordo in ff. lib. 20. 23. & 24. & idcirco ibi ratio ordinis inter haec capita adfetetur. Quod ad primum caput de sponsal. attinet, de eo est titulus 1. de sponsal. est inquam, h. titul 1. quia est generalis. Nam titulus 2. sive titor prov. &c. speciem tenet sponsaliorum: puta est de sponsalibus rectoris provinciae. Quia autem donationes propter nuptias & donat. sponsalitiae, ut & sponsalia plerunque ante nuptias fieri solent, idcirco huic tit. statim adjungitur int. 3. de don. ante nupt. Et & altera hic ratio ordinis, quia tit. 1. de sponsal. agit etiam de minutis fere munusculis, h. e. archiis sponsalitiis & ptoxeneticis. Et haec de primo capite. Caput 2. est ut dixi de nupt. ipsis, quod est trimebre. Nam I adfertur tit. generalis p. tit. 4. de nupt. Deinde adjungitur de nupt. inutil. p. tit. 1. t. de incest. stuprum nupt. Utilia enim prius, inutilia posterius collocanda. Huic adjungitur tit. 6. de interdictio matrim. &c. Ratio est, quia prior est generalior, & de plerisque formis inutiliu nuptiarum, h. tit. 6. unam dutaxat formam sive speciem incestarum nuptiarum continet, puta inter pupillam & tutorem. Hunc sequitur tit. 7. si quacunque, praedium suspectum, &c. quo continetur alia species inutilium nuptiarum, puta inter magistrum provinciae, & provincialem. Ratio, cur haec species sit posterior illa inter tutorem & pupillam, est, quia illa species inter tutorem & pupillam similiter est incestus, in eo, quod tutoris & pupillae sit velut una persona. Huic titulo 7. adjungitur tit. 8. [in] nuptiae ex re[ci]pto, &c. Ratio est quia species inutilium nuptiarum prius sunt exponendae, quam petendae hoc est, subsistentia prior est accidente. III de nuptiis membrum pertinet ad secundas nuptias de quibus est tit. 9. de secundis nuptiis. Ratio est perspicua, quia prius de primis, posteriores de secundis nuptiis agendum. Huc pertinet tit. 10. si cum ... Sed in hoc speciale jus de secundis scilicet nuptiis mulierum continetur. Prius titulus est generalis, & proinde prior. Atque haec de 1 & 2. capite actionis de dote, h.e. sponsalibus & nuptiis I V. est de ipsa dote, ejusque actione, quod quia est caput primarium latius explicatur tit. 13. ut & supra dictum quorum primus est tit. 11. de dotis promissione. Ratio est, quia dos esse non potest, nisi promissa, & ex ea promissione postea nascitur & dos & dotis actio. Statim igitur hunc sequitur titulum 12. de jure dot. in quo de natura dotis & actione de dote tanquam effectu illius promissionis agitur. Cui adjungitur, titulus 13. de rei uxor. act. Nam & hic est de natura dotis. & actione dotis, sed continet jus novum, & proinde est posterior. Recte quoque hoc sequitur titulus 14. de pact. convent. &c. quia actio de dote pactis interdum mutatur & reformatur. Eadem ratio ordinis & supra de contractu emptionis sive actione empti ad tit. de pact. inter empt. & vend. solent enim pacta maxime in continenti adjecta mutare & reformare actionem l. 7. Jurisgentium. §. adeo. de pact. l. nuda. §. penult. de praescript. verb. Praeterea titulus 15. de rei vind. act. lex sive Imp. mutavit actionem tit. 14. pacta privatorum cadem mutant. Lexaurem est potior & prior pactis privatorum. Actionem de dote sequitur exceptio de qua est tit. 15. de doli causa, &c. Ratio est perspicua, exceptio enim sequitur actionem ut ad instit. Huic adjungitur tit. 16. de donat. inter vir. & ux. Ratio ordinis, quia & hic retentio, quae si est similis exceptioni, postea retentio ob res donatas uxori a marito: ita & retentio interdum eidatur contra uxoré dotem petentem, datur, inquam, ex exceptis causis quae olim erant 6 teste Ulp. §. retentiones. lib. reg. quamvis hodie retentiones ilt e fere sunt sublatae per Justin. l. unica. §. taceat. supra de rei ux. ill. Retentionum species una erat, ob res donatas de qua hic est titulus 16 altera erat ob mores de qua est titulus 17. alia ob res amotas, de qua est titulus 21. Etsi autem hae tres species & aliae, ut ob impensas, &c. sunt hodie, ut dictum, sublatae, quia consulitur hodie maritis alia via, quam per retentionem. Quia ergo ipsae retentionum causae sunt sublatae, veterem adhuc ordinem in dispondo C. & ff. ex retentionibus, quae ut dictum exceptioni similes sunt, retinet Tribun Hunc bun. Hunc titulum de donat. inter vir. & uxor. sequitur titul. 17. de repud. & jud. demar. &c. tum quia pertinet ad alteram retentionis causam propter mores, ut jam dictum, tum quia donationes inter virum & uxorem generaliter sunt prohibitæ, ex certis causis valent inter quas est divortium, & proinde post tit. de donat. generalem statim adjungitur tit. de repud. ut posteà tit. 18. de solut. matrim. &c. Uterq; enim est de divortio. Sed prior est de causis & forma, hoc est de natura ipsa divortii, alter tit. nimirum 18. est de eo quod fit per divortium puta repetitio scilicet dotis, quæ non nisi soluto matrimonio repeti potest. Quare regulam, de qua tit. 8. Sequitur statim exceptio, de qua titul. 19. fidos constante matrimonio. Hunc sequitur titul. 20 Ne fidejuss. vel mand. dot. &c. Ratio ordinis est, quia ad repetitionem dotis de qua dict. titul. primori, valde est utilis fidejussor puta ut si maritus, à quo dos repetitur nō fit solvendo saltem ab ejus fidejussore repeti possit. Rectè autem prius de marito & posteà de fidejussore. Huic adjungitur tit. 21. rerum amotar. Ratio ordinis est duplex: tum quia & hæc erat species retentionum, ob res amotas, ut supra dictum Ulp. §. retentiones. tum quia fœminæ divortium cogitantes, plurunq; aliquid amovere solent. Et proinde post divortium ponitur h. tit. l. 2. hujus tit. Est & tertia ratio, quia tit. 20. ne fidejuss. parcatur marito, sive ejus honori, ut hoc tit. 21 parcitur honori fœminæ. Et huic proximus est tit. 22. ne prod. te, &c. tum quia & hic parcitur famæ mariti, quia hoc titul agit de executione actionis, & proinde est ultimus, ut & executi in processu, excepto uno titulo, qui est tit 23. de fundo dot. Ratio, cur hic fit omnium ultimus in hoc tractatu de dote, sive de actione dotis est: quia omnes priores tituli, de actione dotis sunt universales sive de universitate, qualis est dos: hic solus est singularis, puta de fundo dotali, & proinde postremus, & hæc detertio capite. I V. caput est de liberis de quibus est titul. 24. divortio facto apud, &c. & titul 25. de alend. libr. & part. Cur autem ille sit prioris to: ratio hæc est, tum quia ille prioribus titulis est similior, in eo, quod ut priores de divortio ad divortium aliqui pertinent ita & hoc divortio facto, &c. tum quia prius, an & ubi sint educandi, quæri debet quamà quo alantur. Præterea tit. posterior non tantum est de liberis, sed etiam de parentibus. Tractatus autem de parentibus ad matrimonium non pertinet, sed ad liberis, qui sunt fructus matrimonij, pertinet. Sic & infra ubi de tutel. prior est titul. ubi pupil. educar. &c. titulo de ipsis alendis liberis, puta tit. 49. tit. 50. infr. h. lib. 5. & ultimum partim est de concubinis, titul. 26. de concubinis, partim de liberis natuturalibus, titul. 27. de lib. nat. Ratio inter hos 1. titul. est cur de concubinis sit prior, tum quia jus de concubinis est antiquum jus de naturalibus liberis est longè recentius, ab Imp. Constantino introductum Nov. 89. tum quia naturales liberi sunt illi, qui ex concubinis, vel ex ancillis nascuntur. Effectus autem causa sua posterior: Adhuc dictum est de actione dotis, quæ est prior pars hoc libr. 5. & nascitur ex æquo & bono, ut supra dic{ã}um. Huic nunc adjungitur actio tutelæ quæ est altera pars hujus libr. s. sed eadem q. contractu est hoc est tutela sive potius administratione tutelæ. s. tutor. Institut. de obligat. quæ ex q. contract. Ratio exponetur ad ff. ut autem in actione dotis de matrimonio & aliis ad dotem constituendam idoneis ita & hic de tutelis omnia diligenter explicantur. tit. 48. ut supra dictum. Quorum ordo ut fit dilucidior, ad IX. capita erunt revocanda I. continet species tutelæ, de quo est titul.28. & 8. seqq. II. de administratione sive officio tutorum, de quo est tit.37. & 13. seqq. III. est de ipsa act. tutelæ de qua est tit.51. & 7. sequentib. IV. est de auctoritate tutor. tit.9. V. est de finienda tutela. tit.60. & seq. VI. est de excusatione tutorum, tit.62. & 7. seqq. VII. est de curatore furiosi. tit.70. XVIII. est de præjdis minorum, tit.71. & 73. seq. IX. & ultim. est de magistratibus conveniendis, tit.75. & ultim. hoc tit. In ff. quia ordo paulo est alius. ratio ejus erit utrobique explicanda. Et primum quidem de ordine 9. cap. inter se, cur species tutelæ primo exponantur. ratio dicta est supra ad Institut ubi & de secundo capite dictum ad titulum de auctorit. at tutor. Tertij capitis, quod est de Actionibus hæc est ratio, quia actio est effectus administrationis, quæ est quasi contractus, unde hæc actio nascitur. De tel.quiis conjunctionibus capp. dicetur infra ad suum quoque caput. Quod ergo ad singulos tit.
units.tr: So far I have dealt with actions in personam arising from contract, as was said under the Institutes, title "On obligations arising from quasi-contract." But actions in personam arise not only from contract or quasi-contract, from delict or quasi-delict, but also from other causes, such as equity and good faith. Such is the action on dowry, which Cujacius wrongly says arises from contract. For marriage is not a contract, since no contract is made without something given in exchange, and marriage can take place without a dowry, since it is entered into only for the sake of joining persons. Nor is the dowry a contract, since it is a species of gift (l. ult. de donat. ante nupt.), and a gift differs from a contract (l. Aristot. de donat.). Hence the action on dowry does not arise from contract but from equity and good faith, as Gaius rightly says differently (l. 8, ea de cap. min.). Having explained the actions in personam arising from contract, we do not immediately add the actions arising from quasi-contract; rather, the action on dowry is interposed, and it is followed by the action on guardianship, which arises from quasi-contract. These two, I say, dowry and guardianship, are treated throughout this book. The reason for this order, that is, why the action on dowry is placed before the actions on guardianship, will be explained below under the Digest. Since the action on dowry and guardianship are explained under many titles, we will reduce these actions or titles to certain heads, in order to understand the order better. The first action, which concerns dowry, is contained in six heads (capita), and in titles. The first head is on betrothal: title 1 (and 12 and 13 in the second part) concerns betrothal. The second head is on marriage itself, titles 4 and 6 onward. The third head is on the dowry and the action on dowry itself, titles 11 and 12 onward. The fourth head is on children, titles 24 and 25 and the following titles. The order in the Digest, books 20, 23 and 24, is nearly the same, and there the reason for the order among these heads is therefore set out. As for the first head, on betrothal, the title on it is title 1 "On betrothal." I say it is title 1 of this book because it is general. For title 2, "Whether the governor of the province...," holds a species of betrothal, namely betrothals before the governor of the province. And since gifts on account of marriage and gifts on betrothal, and betrothals, are usually made before the marriage, therefore title 3, "On gifts before marriage," is added straight after this title. There is also another reason for the order: title 1 "On betrothal" deals even with small gifts, that is, with betrothal gifts and gifts of the kind called archia and proxenetica. So much for the first head. The second head, as I said, concerns marriage itself, and it has three parts. First, the general title on marriage, title 4, is set down. Next, "On invalid marriages," title 1 (or "On incest and illicit marriage"), follows. For invalid matters should be placed before the others. To this is added title 6, "On the prohibition of marriage," and so on. The reason is that the earlier title is more general and concerns most forms of invalid marriage. Title 6 contains only one form or species of incestuous marriage, namely that between a ward and her guardian. It is followed by title 7, "If anyone should have a suspect dowry," in which another species of invalid marriage is contained, namely between the governor of a province and a woman of the province. The reason this species is placed after the one between guardian and ward is that the marriage between guardian and ward is likewise incest, in that guardian and ward are as it were one person. To this title 7 is added title 8, "On marriage from a ..." The reason is that the species of invalid marriage must be explained before the questions about them, that is, what stands in its own right comes before what is accidental. The third part of the second head, on marriage, concerns second marriages, on which there is title 9, "On second marriages." The reason is clear: what concerns first marriages must be treated before what concerns second marriages. To this belongs title 10, "If with..." But in this place the special law concerning second marriages of women is contained. The earlier title is general and therefore prior. These are the matters of the first and second heads of the action on dowry, that is, betrothal and marriage. The fourth head, the dowry itself and its action, since it is the chief head, is explained more fully in title 13, as also was said above, of which the first is title 11, "On the promise of a dowry." The reason is that there can be no dowry unless it has been promised, and from that promise both the dowry and the action on dowry arise afterwards. Therefore title 12, "On the law of dowry," immediately follows, in which the nature of the dowry and the action on dowry as the effect of that promise are treated. To this is added title 13, "On the action for recovery of a thing given to a wife." For this too concerns the nature of the dowry and the action on dowry, but it contains new law and is therefore later. Rightly also title 14, "On agreements made..." follows this, because the action on dowry is sometimes altered and reshaped by agreements. The same order applies above to the contract of sale, or action of sale, which is joined to the title "On agreements between buyer and seller." For agreements, especially those added at the time, commonly alter and reshape the action (l. 7 Jus gentium §. adeo; de pact.; l. nuda §. penult. de praescript. verb.). Moreover, title 15, "On the action for recovery of property," follows: a law or an imperial constitution has altered the action in title 14, and private agreements do the same. The law is also more powerful and prior to private agreements. The action on dowry is followed by the exception, which is the subject of title 15, "On the cause of fraud," and so on. The reason is clear: an exception follows the action, as stated in the Institutes. To this is joined title 16, "On gifts between husband and wife." The reason for the order is that here too the retention, which is similar to an exception, comes after the retention on account of gifts made by the husband to the wife. So a retention is sometimes also granted against a wife claiming her dowry, that is, it is granted on the excepted grounds which formerly were six, according to Ulpian (§. retentiones, lib. reg.), although today such retentions have almost all been abolished by Justinian (l. unica §. taceat, supra de rei ux. act.). One kind of retention was on account of gifts, the subject of this title 16; another was on account of conduct, the subject of title 17; another on account of goods removed, the subject of title 21. Although these three kinds and others, such as on account of expenses, are, as said, abolished today, since the husband is now provided for by another way than retention, nevertheless, because the causes of retention themselves have been abolished, the Tribonian compilers, in arranging the Code and the Digest, keep the old order concerning retentions, which, as said, are similar to exceptions. After this title "On gifts between husband and wife" comes title 17, "On divorce and the judicial declaration..." partly because it concerns the other ground of retention, on account of conduct, as already said, and partly because gifts between husband and wife are generally prohibited, valid only on certain grounds, among which is divorce. Therefore after the general title "On gifts" there immediately follows the title "On divorce," as afterwards title 18, "On the dissolution of marriage," follows. Both concern divorce. But the first is about the causes and form, that is, the very nature of divorce; the other, namely title 18, concerns what results from divorce, such as the recovery of the dowry, which cannot be recovered unless the marriage has been dissolved. Hence the rule mentioned in title 8 is followed straightaway by the exception of which title 19 treats, "On the dowry while marriage continues." This is followed by title 20, "That a surety or mandator should not..." The reason for the order is that for the recovery of the dowry, treated in the previous title, a surety is very useful, so that if the husband from whom the dowry is recovered is not solvent, at least it can be recovered from his surety. And rightly the husband is treated first, and the surety afterwards. To this is joined title 21, "On goods removed." The reason for the order is twofold: partly because this too was a species of retention, on account of goods removed, as Ulpian said above (§. retentiones); partly because women contemplating divorce commonly remove something. And therefore after divorce this title is placed, and l. 2 of this title. There is also a third reason: as title 20 "That a surety..." spares the husband or his honour, so this title 21 spares the honour of the woman. And next to it is title 22, "That one should not...," partly because here too the reputation of the husband is spared, since this title deals with the execution of the action; and therefore it is last, as also execution comes last in the proceedings, with the exception of one title, which is title 23, "On the dowry land." The reason why this is the very last in this treatise on dowry, or on the action on dowry, is this: all the earlier titles concerning the action on dowry are general, or concern the whole, as the dowry does; this one alone is particular, namely on the dotal land, and therefore it comes last. This is the third head. The fourth head concerns children, on which there is title 24, "On divorce made before..." and title 25, "On the maintenance of children and parents." Why the former precedes: the reason is that partly it is more similar to the earlier titles, in that, as the earlier titles pertain to divorce and to the one in divorce, so does this "On divorce made..." and partly because it must first be asked whether and where children are to be brought up, before asking by whom they are supported. Moreover, the later title concerns not only children but also parents. The treatment of parents does not belong to marriage, but the treatment of children, who are the fruit of marriage, does. So also below, in the title on guardianship, the title "Where the wards are to be educated" comes before the title on the maintenance of children, namely title 49, title 50 below in this book, Book 5, and the last partly concerns concubines, title 26 "On concubines," and partly natural children, title 27 "On natural children." The reason why the first of these titles concerns concubines is that the law on concubines is old, while the law on natural children is much more recent, introduced by the Emperor Constantine (Nov. 89). Natural children are those born of concubines or of maidservants. But an effect is posterior to its cause. So far we have spoken of the action on dowry, which is the first part of this Book 5, and which arises from equity and good faith, as said above. Now there follows the action on guardianship, which is the second part of this book, and which, though it arises from quasi-contract, is rather the administration of guardianship (Institutes, "On obligations arising from quasi-contract," the guardian). The reason will be set out in the Digest. But as with the action on dowry, concerning marriage and the other things suitable for constituting a dowry, so here too all matters concerning guardianships are carefully explained (title 48), as was said above. So that this order may be made clearer, they will be reduced to nine heads. I. The first contains the kinds of guardianship, concerning which there is title 28 and titles 8 onward. II. The second concerns the administration or office of guardians, on which there are titles 37 and 13 onward. III. The third concerns the action of guardianship itself, on which there are titles 51 and 7 onward. IV. The fourth concerns the authority of guardians, title 9. V. The fifth concerns the ending of guardianship, titles 60 onward. VI. The sixth concerns the excuse of guardians, titles 62 and 7 onward. VII. The seventh concerns the curator of a madman, title 70. VIII. The eighth concerns the pledges of minors, titles 71 and 73 onward. IX. And the last concerns the magistrates to be sued, title 75 and the last title of this book. In the Digest the order is somewhat different, and the reason for it will be explained in both places. First, as to the order of the nine heads among themselves: why the kinds of guardianship are set out first, the reason was given above under the Institutes, where also the second head was discussed under the title "On the authority of guardians." The third head, which concerns actions, is for this reason: the action is the effect of the administration, which is like a contract, and from which the action arises. Concerning the remaining heads, the reason will be given further below under their own heads. Now as to the individual titles: first title 28, "On testamentary guardianship," is placed. The reason is set out in the Institutes. To this is joined title 29, "On the confirmation of guardians." The reason will be given in the Digest. Straight after this follows title 30, "On legitimate guardianship," for this is the second kind of guardianship. Why...

units.la: tul. attinet, primo ponitur titul.28. de testament. tutel. Ratio in Institut exposita. Cui adjungitur titul.19. de confirm. tutor. Ratio in ff. afferetur. Eum statim sequitur titul 30. de legit. tut. Est enim hæc secunda tutelæ species. Curita? dictum jam est in Institut. Hunc sequitur tertia quæ est dativa, ad quam pertinet titul.31. & 5. seqq. inter quos 4 titulos de tutela dativa, primus est titul.31. quipetant. tutor. Cur hic primo loco ponatur, hæc est ratio, quia prius tutor petatur quam datur. Ad petitionem quoque pertinet titul.32. ubi petantur tut. &c. Nam prius de eo, qui petat, & posterius de eo, coram quo vel ubi petitur. Reliquis 2. titulis agitur de ipsis tutoribus dativis, qui petuntur sive dantur. Et inter hos prior est titul 33. de tutor. vel curat. allustr. propter dignitatem personæ pupillaris: posterior est titul 34. quasi dare tutor. &c. in quo non tantum de tutoribus, qui dantur, sed etiam de magistratu. qui dat, agitur, quæ etiam causa est cur hic posterior, quia 2. continet. Huic adjungitur titul.35. quandomulier, &c. Adhuc enim de tutore dictum quia tutela vitale munus est, ex leg.2. de regul. jur. sed hic adjungitur exceptio, quæ posterior est regula, quia interdum mater & avia tutelæ officio funguntur ex novis constitutionibus. Hunc sequitur tit.36. in quibus casus. Ratio est, quia priores tituli omnes sunt de primo, hic est de secundo tutore, & proinde posterior, ut supra dictum de restitut. in integrum. titulum si sæpius in integr. Et hæc de primo cap. Proximum est caput de officio tutoris, quod in administratione ponitur. Eò igitur pertinet titul. 37. de administr. tut. qui est 1. in hoc capite, quia est generalis, cui adjungitur tit.38. titulus 38. de peric. tut. Ratio est, quia ex administratione, aut etiam interdum sine ea, tutori est periculum: adhæret scilicet periculum administrationi. Itaque in ff. utrunque sub eodem titulo cōtinetur. Eum sequitur titulus 39. quando ex facto, &c. Nam hic titulus est velut species tituli prioris, qui est de omni periculo, hoc est, tantum de actione: & prior est tantum de tutoris periculo: hic est de pupilli periculo & commodo. Sic & titulus prox. 40. ff. ex plur. tut. &c. Continet speciem tit. de admin. ff. & tut. deperic. & c. Est enim de actione, sed ut prior titulus 39. de actione. quam pupillus exercet vel excipit nomine suo, ita hic titulus 40. est de ea actione, quam tutor exercet vel excipit nomine pupilli. Nam de actione, quæ contra tutorem à minore exercetur quæ est actio tutelæ, dicetur infra. Hoc actionis exercitium, sive pupilli defensio est pars administrationis. Huic titulo adjungitur titulus 41. Ne tut. vel curat. &c. qui tit. quia est prohibitorius, proinde est posterior. Prohibitio autem hæc ad administrationem pertinet, eâ scilicet de causa, ut tutor officiū suū melius faciat, sic & titulus 42. de tut. & curat. qui satis, &c. Est prohibitorius, quia tutor prohibetur prorsus administrare, qui non ante satisdedit. Huic adjungitur tit. 43. de suspect. tut. & curat. Nam & hic est prohibitorius: imo tutor suspectus non tantum prohibetur ab administratione, ut nō satisdans, verum etiam plane removetur, idque interdum cum infamia, quæ quia est pœna, idcirco hic titulus est posterior: quin etiam ratio inter hos titulos prohibitorios ex hac gradatione intelligitur, quod titul 41. prohibetur tutor non administrare sed alienā: titulus 42. prohibetur etiam pupillaria, quod est gravius, titulus 43. prohibetur omnino, quod est gravissimum. Hunc titulum sequitur titulus 44. de in litem dando tutore &c. Ratio est quia administratio, vel est negotiorum, de qua hactenus dictum, vel est litium, de qua hic. Huic adjungitur titulus 45. de eo quo pro tut. &c. Ratio est perspicua, quia hactenus dictum de administratione veri tutoris, nūc de administratione falsi. Hunc sequitur titulus 46. si mater, &c. Ratio est, quia & hic titulus ad titulum de administratione pertinet, puta, si mater indemnitatem promisit, aut alii propinqui. Cui adjungitur titulus 47. si contra matris, &c. hic titulus tantum adjicitur propter mentionem matris jam factam de periculo administrationis. Nam alioquin hic titulus si contra matrem, &c. huc proprie non pertinet. Est enim potius de remotione, quam de administratione tutoris. Huc sequitur tit. 48. ut cause post pub. &c. hac ratione, quia hactenus dictum est de administratione, durante tutela, nunc de ea quæ est finita tutela, sive post pubertatem. Ultimum locum in hoc cap. de officio tutoris obtinet educatio, & alimentorum præstatio, de quibus duobus sunt tit. 49. ubi pupilli educ. & titulus 50. de alimentis pupillo præstand. Ratio ordinis, cur hæc pars officii de educando pupillo postremo loco ponatur, est, quia est tanquam species sive pars officii. Priores autem tituli sunt generales. Specialia sunt generalibus posteriora. Est & altera ratio, quia administratio negotiorum & litium semper tutoribus incumbat, educatio non semper, sed matri saepe & aliis propinquis committitur. l.1. C.h.tit. Inter hos autem duos tit. Cur ille, nisi pupilla educ. &c. prior si altero de alimen. praest. ratio haec est, quia prius semper de loco ubi quid fiat, quam de re ipsa agitur, ut videre est in tit. de jud. ubi quaeritur primum de judice competente, hoc est ubi sit litigandum, & ubi actiones instituendae. Posterius de ipsis actionibus agitur. Et haec hactenus de primo & secundo: hujus tractatus de tutela, postea de ipso tutore & ejus officio, cujus & pars aliqua de auctor. tutor. huc pertinens, rejicitur tamen ad tit. 19. infr. ubi ratio indicabitur. III. Caput de tutelis est de ipsa tutelae actione. Ratio supra expósita est. Est enim haec actio, velut effectus administrationis & proinde posterior, de qua actione est titul. 51. arbitr. tutelae. Hunc sequitur tit. 52. de divid. tut. Ratio ordinis est quia prior tit. est generalis de natura hujus actionis, hic est specialis, puta, si plures sint tutores an ea actione omnes teneantur. Eadem est ratio ordinis in ff. ad titul. de duob. reis qui titulus subsequitur titulum generalem de verbor. obl. Ad hanc actionem tutelae pertinet tit. 53. de in lit. jur. Ratio, quia priores tituli sunt de hac actione sive ejus natura, cui, contra quem detur: hic jam est de ea exercenda an scilicet in ea in litem juretur. Quaero, cur hic titul. ad actionem tutelae hic in Cod accommodetur, cum in litem jusjurandum etiam ad alias actiones pertineat. Ratio haec est quia in litem jusjurandum in actione tutelae maxime praestaturad versus heredes tutoris, leg.1. Cod. de tulit. jur. Ideoque titulus de hered. tut. qui est 54. hic adjungitur: nam postquam de ipso tutore, qui hac actione tutelae tenetur, actum est, proximum est de hiisce ejus heredibus explicare. Itaque hi duo tituli 53. & 54. recte hic conjunguntur. Prior tamen est de in lit. jurand. quia hoc jusjurandum etsi plerunque contra heredem, interdum tamen etiam contra ipsum tutorem praestatur, leg.2. C.hoc tit. Huic titulo, ne heredib. tutor. jam adjungitur titul. 55. si tutor non geffer. Nam & hic pertinet ad actionem tutelae sed quia prius agendum est de tutore, qui gessit, an teneatur haec actione, subsequitur recte de tutore, qui non gessit; nam & hic tenetur. His de actionibus titulis adjungutur duo tituli accessorii, puta tit. 56. de usur. p: p. & tit. 57. de fid. juss. tut. & c. Notum est, usuram & fidejussores jure dici accessiones. Accessoria autem principalibus sunt posteriora. Cur autem titulus de usur. sit prior eo, qui est de fidejussor. Ratio haec est: quia ut priores tituli ad tutorem, sed de re principali, pupillorum: ita & hic quoque titulus ad tutorem pertinet, sed est de usuris. Ratio autem postulat, ut prius agatur de tutore, hoc est re principali, quam de accessorio, sive tutoris fidejussore. Hunc titul. de fidejussor. tut. sequitur titul. 58. de contraria jud. c. Prius scilicet de directo agendum fuit, posterius de contrario tutelae judicio, ut & in ff. ratio postulat. Et haec de tertio capite. IV. Est de auctoritate.
units.tr: As far as the titles of this chapter are concerned, first comes title 28, de testament. tutel., whose rationale is set out in the Institutes. To it is joined title 19, de confirm. tutor., whose rationale will be given in the Digest. Immediately after it comes title 30, de legit. tut., since this is the second species of guardianship. Why it is ordered this way has already been explained in the Institutes. After it comes the third species, the dative guardianship, to which title 31 and the following titles, 5 in all, belong. Of these four titles on dative guardianship, the first is title 31, quipetant. tutor. The reason it is placed first is that a guardian must be sought before he is given. To the seeking also belongs title 32, ubi petantur tut. &c., since first comes the person who seeks, and afterwards the person before whom, or the place where, he is sought. The remaining two titles deal with the dative guardians themselves, who are sought or given. Of these, the earlier is title 33, de tutor. vel curat. allustr., on account of the dignity of the ward's person. The later is title 34, quasi dare tutor. &c., which treats not only of the guardians who are given but also of the magistrate who gives them. This is also the reason the latter comes later: it contains two matters. To it is added title 35, quandomulier, &c., since guardianship is still under discussion, being a personal office, according to leg. 2. de regul. jur. But here an exception is added, which is the later rule, because sometimes a mother and a grandmother discharge the office of guardian under the new constitutions. There follows title 36, in quibus casus. The reason is that the earlier titles all concern the first guardian, while this one concerns the second guardian, and so it comes later, as said above under de restitut. in integrum, title si sæpius in integr. And so much for the first chapter. The next chapter is on the office of the guardian, which is set out under administration. To it therefore belongs title 37, de administr. tut., which comes first in this chapter because it is general. To it is joined title 38, de peric. tut. The reason is that from administration, or sometimes even without it, the guardian is exposed to risk: risk clings to administration. Accordingly, in the Digest both are contained under the same title. There follows title 39, quando ex facto, &c. For this title is in a way a species of the earlier title, which concerns every risk, that is, only the action; the earlier concerns only the guardian's risk, while this one concerns the risk and advantage of the ward. So too the next title, 40, ff. ex plur. tut. &c., contains a species of the titles de admin. and de tut. de peric. &c. For it concerns an action, but just as title 39 concerns the action which the ward brings or receives in his own name, so this title 40 concerns the action which the guardian brings or receives in the name of the ward. For the action brought by the minor against the guardian, which is the action of guardianship, will be discussed below. This exercise of an action, or the defence of the ward, is part of administration. To this title is joined title 41, ne tut. vel curat. &c., which, being prohibitory, comes later. This prohibition, however, belongs to administration, namely for this reason: that the guardian may discharge his office better. So too title 42, de tut. & curat. qui satis, &c., is prohibitory, because a guardian who has not first given security is forbidden to administer at all. To this is joined title 43, de suspect. tut. & curat. For this too is prohibitory: indeed a suspect guardian is not merely forbidden to administer, as one who has not given security is, but is actually removed altogether, sometimes with infamy. Since this is a penalty, the title comes later. Indeed the order among these prohibitory titles can be understood from this gradation: under title 41 the guardian is forbidden to administer the property of another; under title 42 he is forbidden also to administer the ward's property, which is more serious; under title 43 he is forbidden altogether, which is most serious. After this title comes title 44, de in litem dando tutore &c. The reason is that administration is either of affairs, which has been discussed so far, or of lawsuits, which is what is treated here. To this is joined title 45, de eo quo pro tut. &c. The reason is plain: what has been said so far concerns the administration of a true guardian, and now comes that of a false one. There follows title 46, si mater, &c. The reason is that this title too belongs to the title on administration, for example if the mother or other relatives have promised indemnity. To it is joined title 47, si contra matris, &c. This title is added only because of the mention of the mother already made regarding the risk of administration. Otherwise this title, si contra matrem, &c., does not properly belong here, for it concerns the removal of a guardian rather than his administration. There follows title 48, ut cause post pub. &c., for this reason: what has been said so far concerns administration while guardianship lasts, and now comes that which follows the end of guardianship, that is, after puberty. The last place in this chapter on the office of the guardian is held by the upbringing and the provision of maintenance, concerning which there are two titles, 49, ubi pupilli educ., and title 50, de alimentis pupillo præstand. The reason for the order, why this part of the office, the bringing up of the ward, is placed last, is that it is, as it were, a species or part of the office. The earlier titles are general, and specific titles come after general ones. There is also a second reason: administration of affairs and of lawsuits always rests upon the guardians, whereas upbringing does not always rest on them but is often committed to the mother and other relatives (l. 1. C. h. tit.). Between these two titles, why nisi pupilla educ. &c. comes before de alimen. praest., the reason is this: the question of the place where something is to be done is always treated before the matter itself, as can be seen in the title de jud., where first the competent judge is asked about, that is, where the suit is to be brought and where the actions are to be instituted; afterwards the actions themselves are treated. And so much for the first and second parts. The treatise on guardianship is now followed by the guardian himself and his office, of which a part also belongs here, de auctor. tutor., though it is nevertheless referred to title 19 below, where the reason will be indicated. III. The third chapter on guardianship concerns the action of guardianship itself. The reason has been set out above. For this action is, as it were, the effect of administration, and therefore comes later. Concerning this action is title 51, arbitr. tutelae. There follows title 52, de divid. tut. The reason for the order is that the earlier title is general, concerning the nature of this action, while this one is specific, for example whether, if there are several guardians, all are bound by this action. The same reason of order holds in the Digest under the title de duob. reis, which follows the general title de verbor. obl. To this action of guardianship belongs title 53, de in lit. jur. The reason is that the earlier titles concern this action, or its nature, its object, and against whom it is given; this one now concerns its exercise, namely whether one is to swear to the amount in the suit. I ask why this title on the action of guardianship is placed here in the Code, since the oath on the amount in the suit pertains also to other actions. The reason is that the oath on the amount is chiefly exacted in the action of guardianship against the heirs of the guardian (l. 1. Cod. de tutel. jur.). Therefore title 54, de hered. tut., is joined here: for after the guardian himself, who is bound by this action of guardianship, has been treated, it is next to explain his heirs. Thus these two titles, 53 and 54, are rightly joined here. The former, however, is de in lit. jurand., because although this oath is generally exacted against the heir, it is sometimes exacted also against the guardian himself (l. 2. C. hoc tit.). To this title, ne heredib. tutor., is now joined title 55, si tutor non gesserit. For this too belongs to the action of guardianship, but since it must first be settled whether the guardian who acted is bound by this action, it rightly follows with the guardian who did not act, for he too is bound. To these titles on actions are joined two accessory titles, namely title 56, de usur. pup., and title 57, de fid. juss. tut. &c. It is well known that interest and sureties are called accessories in law. But accessories come after principal matters. Why the title de usur. comes before that de fidejussor. is for this reason: as the earlier titles concern the guardian, but concern the principal matter, the property of the wards, so this title too concerns the guardian, but it is about interest. The reason, however, requires that the guardian be treated first, that is, the principal matter, before the accessory, or the guardian's surety. After the title de fidejussor. tut. comes title 58, de contraria jud. c. For first the direct matter had to be treated, and afterwards the contrary judgment of guardianship, as the Digest's order also requires. And so much for the third chapter. IV. It concerns authority.

units.la: Tit.II. Tit.III. Tit.IIII. Tit.IV. Tit.V. Tit.VI. Tit.VII. Tit.VIII. tate tutorum, de qua tantum est tit. 59. de auctor. praestand. Ratio ordinis obscurior est, quia cum auctoritas sit pars quaedam officii, rectius ad caput secundum, ubi de administratione, hic titulus pertinere videtur, ut & in ff. Ratio tamen hic in Cod. est; tum quia auctoritas differt ab administratione, ut est apud Ulp. infrag. lit. II. §. tutoris; tum quia auctoritas tutoris necessaria est non tantum in negotiis & litibus, sed etiam in ipsa actione tutelae instituenda. l. pen. C. si adversus remiss. & c. tum quia auctoritas non interponitur in eo, quod finit tutelam. l. ult. verf. sed & omnia, C. hoc tit. Et proinde hic tit de auctoritate recte anteponitur capiti. V. quod est de finienda tutela, sub quo est tit. 62. quando tut. vel curat. esse desin. Hic quoque pertinet tit. 61 de actore atut. dand. Nam in loco tutoris non quidem finita, sed tantum quasi finita tutela, hoc est, in loco tutoris impediti ad administrandum, solet hic actor dari, §. ultim. Inst. de tut.
units.tr: Titles II to VIII... on the authority of guardians, which is treated only in title 59, de auctoritate praestanda. The order of the chapter is rather obscure, because authority is a part of the office, so this title would seem more properly to belong to the second chapter, where administration is treated, as also in the Digest. Nevertheless the Code places it here, for three reasons: (1) authority differs from administration, as Ulpian says in the Institutes, book 2, §. tutoris; (2) a guardian's authority is needed not only in business and lawsuits but also in bringing the guardianship action itself, l. pen. C. si adversus remiss. etc.; (3) authority is not interposed in what ends the guardianship, l. ult. verf. sed & omnia, C. hoc tit. Accordingly this title on authority is rightly placed before the fifth chapter, on ending guardianship, under which is title 62, quando tut. vel curat. esse desin. Title 61, de actore tutoris dando, also belongs here. For in the place of a guardian who is not indeed finished but only as it were finished, that is, in the place of a guardian prevented from administering, an agent is usually appointed, §. ultim. Inst. de tut.

units.la: V I. Caput vocavimus de excusatione tutorum, quod prioricapiti de finienda tutela statim adjungitur, hac ratione, quia excusatio est quaedam species finiendae tutelae. §. ult. Inst. quib. mod sin. tut.
units.tr: VI. We have called the sixth chapter the chapter on the excuse of guardians. It is immediately joined to the preceding chapter on ending guardianship, for this reason: excuse is a certain kind of ending of guardianship, §. ult. Inst. quib. mod. sin. tut.

units.la: In hoc autem capite tit. 62. de excus. & tempor. earum, est primus, quia generalis: Cui adjungitur tit. 63. si sal. & c. Nam & hic est generalis: sed ille posterior: quia ille est de natura excusationum & de verbis calumniae sive allegationibus, hic est de falsis. Hos sequuntur tituli speciales quorum i. est titul. 4 si tut. vel curator Reip. abef. & c. Ratio est quia haec species sive causa excusationis, puta absentia Reipub. causa, est publica. Cuiadjungitur tit 65. d. excus. Ulteran. & c. Nam militia est velut absentia Reip. causa. Huic proximus est tit 66. quinum. lib. se excus. & c. Ratio quia & haec excusatio ut 2. priores, valde est favorabilis, & ad utilitatem publicam pertinet liberorum procreatio, & multitudo. Sic & morbus est causa favorabilis, sed posterior, quia privata de quo est tit. 67. qui morbo se excus. Cui adjungitur tit. 68. quaerave, & c. hoc est, senectute se excusant, quae & ipsa est velut morbus, ut vulgo dicitur, Aristoteles f. de gener. an. cap. 4. & quia ad mortem accedit recte prioribus causis est posterior. Ultimum locum hic obtinet excusatio, propter tres tutelas sive numerum tutelarum, tit. 69. qui numero tutelarum, tum quia haec causa differt ab aliis prioribus in eo, quod priores excusent ab omni tutela, haec tantum excusat a quarta, tum quia haec non semper excusat, ne a quarta quidem, si quis tres affectarit, sive affectatione fuerit. Sic enim legendum est hic ubi vulgo est defunctorie, l. 15. §. ult. de excus. tut. & haec de sexto capite. Ad VII pertinet tit. 70. de curat. furiosi. Ratio est, quia priora sex capita sunt de tutore vel curatore pupillorum vel minorum: hoc caput est de curatore furiosi aut prodigi, qui curatores sunt majorum: & proinde posteriores, ut ipsa aetas major posterior minore. IIX. Caput de praediis minorum non alienandis sine decreto judicis in ff. contrarius est ordo. Ubi ratio ordinis exponetur. Hujus igitur capitis de praediis primus titulus est tit. 71. de praediis & aliis rebus minorum sine decreto non alien-vel oblig.qui est generalis, quæ sequitur tit.72.quando decreto opiu non sit,&c. Ratio est, quia prior est de eo, quádo est opus, hic quando nô. Affirmatio autem natura est prior negatione, ut sup. dictû ad lib.2.tit.40. Et velut exceptio quædam h.titu.72. continetur, & proinde tanquam generalis ponitur ante tit.73.si quis ignorans, rem minoris esse sine decreto, copaverit, quo tantum species exceptionis adfertur. Hunc sequitur tit.74.si major factu.&c. quo etiam velut exceptio adfertur, qua alieuatio absq; decreto facta valeat, seu rata maneat. Restat nonû & ultimum caput de tutelis, quod est de actione subsidiaria, de quo capite est tit.75.de magistrat. conven. Ratio exponetur infra ad ff. Et hæc de titulis Libri V. Codicis.
units.tr: In this chapter, title 62, de excusationibus et temporibus earum, comes first, because it is general. To it is joined title 63, si sal. etc. For this too is general, but the former is the later one, because the former deals with the nature of excuses and with the wording of objections or pleas, while this one deals with false ones. These are followed by special titles, of which the first is title 64, si tutor vel curator reipublicae causa absit etc. The reason is that this kind of excuse, namely absence on account of the Republic, is public. To it is joined title 65, de excusationibus ulterius etc., for military service is as it were absence on account of the Republic. Next to this is title 66, quinum liberos habens se excusat etc. The reason is that this excuse, like the two earlier ones, is very favourable, and the procreation and multitude of children pertain to public benefit. Illness is likewise a favourable cause, but a later one, because it is private; it is treated in title 67, qui morbo se excusat. To it is joined title 68, quaeve etc., that is, those who excuse themselves on account of old age, which is itself like an illness, as is commonly said (Aristotle, De gener. an., c. 4). And since old age approaches death, it is rightly placed after the earlier causes. The last place in this chapter is held by the excuse on account of three guardianships, or the number of guardianships, title 69, qui numero tutelarum. This is so, first, because this cause differs from the earlier ones in that those excuse from all guardianship, whereas this excuses only from a fourth; and second, because this does not always excuse, not even from a fourth, if someone has aimed at three guardianships. For so it must be read here, where the common text has "perfunctorily" (defunctorie), l. 15. §. ult. de excus. tut. And this is said concerning the sixth chapter.

units.la: Lib. VI. Codicis.

units.la: NUnc de libro sexto videamus. Cujus lib.ti.62. possunt commode ad f mƲbrarevocari I.est de actione furti. II. de actione operarû aliisq; ad jura patronorû & libertorû pertinentib. III. de bonorû possessione. IV. est de hereditate, tã ex testamento, q ab intestato. V. est accessorium Ordo horum capitû atq; totius libri satis ... multi non assequuntur. Exordine Edicti perpetui intelligi potest q Edictum Tribun. in Cod. magis q in ff. sequitur, ut jã ante dictum. Ordo igitur edicti fuit iste (res n. paulo altius est repetenda) ut in edicto primû ponerētur civilia deinde prætoriarum & judicia quia civilia prætoriis sunt præstantiora ut & alias dictû. Et hûc ordinem tenuit Trib. tã in ff. q in Cod. licet interdum ab eo discedat, ut supra admonuimus. Eaa. judicia q hactenus exposuimus, pleraq; sunt civilia, exceptis paucis prætoriis q propter similitudinem fuerunt civilibus adjuncta. Nunc ratio postulat, ut explicatis civilib. transeamus ad ptoria: quorû initiû fuit in edicto ab actione furti, aut certè à bonorû possessione. Actio furti est quodámodo media partim civilis de furto nec manifesto, partim ptoria, de furto manifesto. §. sunt autem, Inst. de nox. act. sed in his prætoriis judiciis persequendis, & ordine tractandis sæpe Trib. discediat ab ordine edicti perpetui, multaq; interjicit certis de causis, quas suo loco exponemus. Ex his jã intelligitur, cur hoc libro de actione furti statim initio hujus lib.tit.2.de furtis & servo corrupt. agatur. Ratio est, quia actio furti actioni rationib. distrahendis, q ad tutelas pertinet, valde est similis, adeo ut tutor, si res pupilli distrahat animo furandi nô tantum actione rationib. distrahendis, sed etiã furti teneatur, l.1.§.pen.l.2.de tut.& ratio.distrah. Et hunc ordinem ut actionē rationib. distrahendis, statim sequeretur, actio furti fuisse in Edicto perpetuo, itéid, q dixi supra in Edicto primo; civilia post prætoria fuisse collocata, perspicuû est ex legib. Caji & Pauli ad Edictum, & etiã ex Paulo lib.2.sent.tit.30. & seq. Cur autem titulus de furt. hic præcedat tit.de serv.fugitiv.&c. qui est primus hujus libri, hæc est ratio, quia furtum est plerunq; servorû. Duo enim sunt servorum vitia frequentia & conjuncta fuga & furtum; & fugæ est prior, quia docet furtum, quod est velut discipulus fugæ, ut eleganter Martialis; Huicquoq; est ꝓ olim in seruorum venditionib. cautio adhiberi solet, fugitiu̅, furé non esse l.1. de edil. edict. ut & Cujac. in Para. Cur autem subtic. 2. adjungatur de seruo corrupto, ratio est ꝑ pter similitudinem argumenti. Nā & fuga & furtum sunt vitia & corruptelæ seruorū. nec modo dictum. Et hæc de primo capite hujus libri ꝗ est de actione furti, & de actione serui corrupti, ꝗ duæ actiones in ff longo intervallo disjungūtur. Alterum caput est de actione operarū, de quo est tit. 3. cū s. seqq. Ratio quia & in Edicto perpetuo, ꝓ & in C. diligeter imitatur. idem fuerit ordo, vt actionem furti sequeretur actio operarū liberti. Ratio videtur, tū quia servi & liberti conditiones sunt vicinæ, & hic illū sequitur: quia ex servo manumiss. fit libertus) tum quia operarum negatio, est velut furti species. Et hæc est ratio ordinis adtit. 3 de Tit. III. oper. libert. in Cod. Nam in ff (in quib. Tribunianus sæpè longius discedit à ratione Edicti perpetui) & alio loco & alia ratione hæc actio operarum ponitur Huic titulo de oper. liber. adjungit Tribun. alios titulos ad libertos & jus patronorū pertinentes: hac ni fallor ratione, utromnia patroni juraad libertos ptinentia anno eodem; loco explicētur Sunt aut 3. ferè jura patroni, ꝗ ei à liberto veniunt operæ, bona, & obsequiū sive reverentia. De operis agitur tit. 3. ut jā dictum de bonis agitur tit.4. de bon. liber. Ratio cur ptinus de Tit.IV. operis, posterius de bonis agat est. tum ꝗa operarū negatio est similis furto, de quo priùs: tū quia operæ omnino patrono debētur intellige, si promissæ sunt, bona non sæpe nec omnia, tū deniq; quia de bonis novū jus adfertur, & pinde posterius. Ad hunc tit. de bon. liber. pertinet, tit.5. si in frau. patr. ḉc. Tit. V. Nā est de alienatione bonorū. Sed tit.14. est generalis, ideoq; prior. Ut aut de operis est actio operarū ita & de bonis est actio Faviana vel Calbisiana, si alienentur in fraudē. Dictū est de operis, & de bonis. Tertiū est obsequiū, de quo est tit. 6. de obseq. ḉc. ꝓ quia minimum est, postremum locū tenet. Nam oblē- Tit. VI. quiū est tantum reue rentiæ munus l.5. hoc tit. Ei ꝑ vimus est tit.7. d. liber. ḉ- Tit.VII. eor. liber. qui tit nō est ita generalis, ut verba sonàr sed est potius specialis, de libertis scil. ingratis ubi & actio est contra ingratos libertos eorumq; liberos. ꝓ velut crimen ingrati merito posteriorem locum tenet. Sed ultimū tamen locum in hoc capite secundo, quod est de actione ingrati, & libertis renet tit.8. de jure aureorū annulorum, ḉc. Ratio est, quia ad hiniendā libertini- Tit. VIII. tatē pertinet. Duo n. sunt modi, quib. definit esse libertus & liberatur illis tribus: operis, bonis & obsequiis puta jus aureorū annulorum, & natalium restitutio. III. Hujus libri caput est de bonorū possessionib. quod hic 12. tit. continetur: Cur aut hoc loco de bonorum possessionibus agitur, ratio ordinis ex Edicto sumenda est, in quo post civilia, (de quibus lib.3. ḉ 4 Prætoria erant dispositā ut supra dictum, & ita quidem, ut actionem de furto sequerentur Edicta de bonorum possessionibus, adeo ut primum fere inter prætoria locū haberent bonorum possessiones. Quid ita? quia universitatem cōtinent: Universalia singularibus sunt priora, ut supra dictum. Quod de Edicti ordine dicitur, confirmatur ex lib.6.IC. ad Edict.ex lib.2.& 3.sent.Paul. In hoc igitur tertio capite de bon. poss. merito est primus tit. 9.qui admitti ad bonorum possessionem possunt §.intra quod t mpus. Quia generalis, cujus velut pars est tit.10.quando non petentium,&c. Agit enim de jure adcrescendi,quod tantum locum habet inter plures bonorum possessores. In ff. hoc de jure adcrescendi comprehensum est sub titulo generali, de bon.poss. Hos duos tit-ulos generales, sequuntur alij speciales, & primus quidem, tit. 11. de bon. poss.sic.tab. & hunc tit 12. de bon.poss.cont.tab. In ff.& Inst. contrarius est ordo. Ratio ff.infra adferetur In C.autem ratio ordinis haec videtur,cur inquit hic secundum tabulas priorfit illo contra tabulas, tum quia secundum tabulam est favorabilior, contra tabulam est odiosior, ut oppugnans testamentum:tum quia tit.13. de poss.cont.tab.l berti, quae patronis vel liberis eorum datur. Optime convenit tit.12 Nam utroque continetur bonorum possessio contra tabulas, una quae datur liberis contra tabulas parentum. tit.12. altera quae datur patronis eorumque liberis, contra tabulas liberti titu.13. Cui adjungitur tit.14. Unde liberi. & hinc 15.Unde legit.mi,& unde cogn. & huic 16.de succeff.or. Edict. Ratio exponetur ad ff.ubi idem ordo. Huic tit.16. adjungitur 17.de Carbon.Edict. tantum propter mentionem, ut puto Edicti in utroque tit. Tandem adjungitur tit.18. Unde vir & ux. Quia ex 4.bon. possab intestato haec est ultima. ex ratione juris. Hunc sequitur tit. 19. de repud.bon.poss. Ratio ordinis est, quia prius est,ut de natura bon. poss. eaque adquirenda posterius de repudiandaagitur Ultimus in hoc capite tertio titulus est 20.de col. quia collocatio demum fiat post petitam jam bon.poss.l.ii. hujus tit. Sed in eo migravit Tribun.ordinem Edicti de quo infra. Et haec de tertio capite hujus libri sexti. I V. Caput est de hereditate quod trimembre facimus Vel enim est de hereditate ex testamento, de quo est titul.21.& 15. seqq.vel est de legatis & fideicommissis, de quibus tit.37.&17. seqq. Tertium est de hereditate ab intestato, de quo est tit.55.de suis & legit. & 4. seqq. Quod ad rationem ordinis attinet, hoc est, cur bonorum possessio (de qua cap.3. hujus libri) ponatur ante hereditatem (de qua est caput hoc 4.) ea pendet ex Edicto perpetuo, in quo idem fuit ordo ut prius de bon.poss. quam de testamento ageretur. Ratio autem Edicti, licet obscurior, haec mihi videtur, idque propterea, quod testamenta fere sint civilia, & ex legibus XII. Tab. pendeant,nempe illa; Utiq; legassit,&c. Dictum autem est supra in Edicto primum locum fuisse tributum praetoriis, inter quae bonorum possessio praecipuum locum tenet. Erant quidem in Edicto quaedam ad testamenta quoque pertinentia, sed pauca,& quae ad bonorum possessionem accommodari possint eique etiam serviant. ut Edictum, siquis omissa causa testamenti, &c.Ut cautio legatorum,&c.l.6.ut quis omissa causa testamenti,&c. Ut Edictum de testamentis aperiendis.quod Edictum de bon.poss. petinon poterit, nisi testamento aperto. Atque ideo in Edicto perpetuo tit. de bon. poss. statim sequebatur Edict. sive tit. de tab. test. aperr. quia ut modo dictum, bonorum possessio peti aut repudiari non potest nisi tabulae aperiantur. Et hac de ratione ordinis ad hoc caput, quod dixi esse trimembre, de testamento, de legatis, de causa inte stati Ratio autem ordinis iuter haec tria membra, partim jam supra est expositaad Instit partim ex iis, quae infra intelligetur. Nunc de singulis, hujus trimembris capitis titulis qui sunt 39. videamus. Quod ad primum membrum de testamentis attinet, in eo primus est tit. 21. de test. milit. proximus scilicet tit. de collat. de quo jam dictum. Ratio, cur hoc in membro de testamentis titulus sit de test. milit. cum alius sit ordo in Inst. & ff haec est, quia ut saepe jam dictum Tribun. in C. maxime sequitur ordinem, edicti perpetui, in quo Edicto species bonorum possessionis fuit, quae dicitur ex testamento milit. Et proinde hic titulus statim sequitur priorem tractatum de bon. poss. Dices, cur ergo hunc titulum non refers ad caput tertium, quod est de bonorum possessionibus sed ad caput quartum, quod est de hereditatibus sive testamentis? Ratio est, quia Tribunianus eum ita accommodavit, & inscripsit de testamento, & non de bonorum poss. ex testamento militis Ordinem igitur Edicti spectavit, licet rem non spectet, hoc est bonorum possessionem, sed hereditatem. Huic adjungitur tit 22. qui testamenta fac. poss. & eum titu. 23. de testamentis. Ratio ordinis exponetur ad ff. Primo enim de ipsis testamentis, hoc est, de testatione & forma agitur, proximum est de heredibus, l. 2. ff. qui test. fac. poss. Itaq; hos duos titulos (qui in ff uno continentur) statim sequitur tit. 24. de hered. instit. & 5. tituli seqq. qui omnes sunt de heredibus, quorum primus est, ut dixi, de heredibus instituendis generalis. Huic subjungitur tit 25. de instit. & substit. hac ratione, quia hic agitur de heredibus sub conditione institutis aut substitutis: Prior autem titulus est de heredibus pure institutis. Puta, conditionali institutione est plenior & perfectior, ideoque prior. Hunc sequitur tit. 26. de impub. & al. subst. Ratio ordinis ad Instit. est expositia Proximus est tit 27. de necess. hered. & c. Ratio enim dignitatis postulat, ut prius de heredibus liberis, posterius de heredibus servis agatur. Tandem hunc sequitur tit. 28. de lib. praeter. & exher. Ratio est, quia priores tituli sunt de institutione, hic est de exheredatione, quae est odiosa, & proinde posterior. Ultimus de heredibus est tit. 29. de posthum. hered. instit. quia posthumi nihil aliud sunt, quam posteri. Recte autem hic titulus de posthumis heredib. adjungitur priori titulo, de lib. praeter. quia & hic titulus est de liberis, sed prior est de jam natis, hic de nondum natis, hoc est, posthumis: Et quia exheredatio pertinet ad utrosque natos & posthumos, sed non ad heredes extraneos. Dictum est in hoc primo membro de testatore & forma testamenti & herede: Restat tertia hujus membri pars de ipsa hereditate ex testamento, quia scilicet est effectus testamenti. & proinde haec pars est posterior. Et primo quidem de hereditate adeunda sive adquirenda agitur, puformam sive speciem incestarum nuptiarum continet, puta inter pupillam & tutorem. Hunc sequitur tit. 7. si quacunque, prad. tutspo*esl.are, &c. quo continetur alia species inutilium nuptiarum, puta inter magistrum provinciae, & provincialem. Ratio, cur haec species sit posteriori illa inter tutorem & pupillam est, quia illa species inter tutorem & pupillam similiter est incestus, in eo quod tutoris & pupillae sit velut una persona. Huic titulo 7. adjungitur tit. 8. si nuptiae exre(ci)pto, &c. Ratio est quia species inutilium nuptiarum prius sunt exponendae, quam petendae hoc est, tubstantia prior est accidente. III de nuptiis membrum pertinet ad secundas nuptias de quibus est l. 9. d. secund. nupt. Ratio est perspicua, quia in hoc de primis, posteriores de secundis nuptiis agendum. Huc pertinet & tit. 10. Si cum lo nuptae erit mulier, &c. Sed in hoc speciale jus de secundis scilicet nuptiis mulierum continetur. Prius titulus est generalis, & proinde prior. Atque haec de 1 & 2. capite actionis de dote, h.e. iponsalibus & nuptiis I V. est de ipsa dote, ejusque actione, quod quia est caput primarium latius explicatur tit. 13. ut & supra dictum quorum primus est tit. 11. de dotis promiss. Ratio est, quia dos esse non potest, nisi promissa, & ex ea promissione postea nascitur & dos & dotis actio. Statim igitur hunc sequitur titulum 12. de jure dot. in quo de natura dotis & actione de dote tanquam effectu illius promissionis agitur. Cui adjungitur, titulus 3. de rei ux. act. Nam & hic est de natura dotis. & actione dotis, sed continet jus novum, & proinde est posterior. Recte quoque hoc sequitur titulus 14. de pact. convent. &c. quia actio de dote pactis interdum mutatur & reformatur. Eadem ratio ordinis & supra de contractu emptionis sive actione empti ad tit. de pact. int. empt. & vend. solent enim pacta maxime in continenti adjecta mutare & reformare actionem l. 7. Jur. gentium. §. adeo. de pact. l. nuda. §. penult. de praescript. verb. Praeterea titulus 13. de rei ux. act. lex sive Imp. mutavit actionem tit. 14. pacta privatorum eadem mutant. Lex autem est potior & prior pactis privatorum. Actionem de dote sequitur exceptio de quaest. tit. 15. de dote causa, &c. Ratio est perspicua, exceptio enim sequitur actionem ut ad instit. Huic adjungitur titul. 16. de donat. inter vir. & ux. Ratio ordinis, quia & hic retentio, quae si est similis exceptioni, postea retentio ob res donatas uxori a marito: ita & retentio iuterdum eidatur contra uxoris dotem petentem, datur, inquam, ex exceptis causis quae olim erant 6 teste Ulp. §. retentiones lib. reg. quamvis hodie retentiones ist e fere sunt sublatae per Justin. l. unica. ff. taceat. supra de rei ux. act. Retentionum species una erat, ob res donatas de qua hic est titulus 16 altera erat ob mores de qua est titulus 17. alia ob res amotas, de qua est titulus 21. Etsi autem hae tres species & aliae, ut ob impensas, &c sunt hodie, ut dictum, sublatae, quia consulitur hodie maritis alia via, quam per retentionem. Quia ergo ipsae retentionum causae sunt sublatae, veterem adhuc ordinem in disponendo C. & ff. ex retentionibus, quae ut dictum exceptioni similes sunt, retinet Tribunus Hunc bun. Hunc titulum de donat. inter vir. & c. sequitur titul. 17. de repud. & jud. de mar. &c. tum quia pertineat ad alteram retentionis causam propter mores, ut jam dictum, tum quia donationes inter virum & uxorem generaliter sunt prohibitæ, ex certis causis valent inter quas est divortium, & proinde post tit. de donat. generalem statim adjungitur tit. de repud. ut postea tit. 18. solut. matrim. &c. Uterq; enim est de divortio. Sed prior est de causis & forma, hoc est de natura ipsa divortii, alter tit. nimirum 18. est de eo quod fit per divortium puta repetitio scilic. dotis, quæ non nisi soluto matrimonio repeti poterit. Quare regulam, de qua tit. 8. Sequitur statim exceptio, de qua titul. 19. fidos constante matrimonio. Hunc sequitur titul. 20. Ne fidejuss. vel mand. dot. &c. Ratio ordinis est, quia ad repetitionem dotis de qua dict. titul. priori, valde est utilis fidejussor puta. ut si maritus, à quo dos repetitur nō sit solvendo saltem ab ejus fidejussore repeti possit. Rectè autem prius de matrimonio et postea de fidejussore. Huic adjungitur tit. 21. rerum amotar. Ratio ordinis est duplex: tum quia & hæc erat species retentionum, ob res amotas, ut supra dictum Ulp. ff. retentiones. tum quia fœminæ divortium cogitantes, plurimum aliquid amovere solent. Et proinde post divortium ponitur h. tit. l. 2. hujus tit. Est & tertia ratio, quia tit. 20. ne fideiuss. parcatur marito, sive ejus honori, ut hoc tit. 21. parcitur honori fœminæ. Et huic proximus est tit. 22. ne prod. te, &c tum quia & hic parcitur famæ mariti, quia hoc titul agit de executione actionis, & proinde est ultimus, ut & executi in processu, excepto uno titulo, qui est tit 23. de fundo dot. Ratio, cur hic sit omnium ultimus in hoc tractatu de dote, sive de actione dotis est: quia omnes priores tituli, de actione dotis sunt universales sive de universitate qualis est dos: hic solus est singularis, puta de fundo dotali, & proinde postremus, & hæc deteritio capite. I V. caput est de liberis de quibus est titul. 24. divortio facto apud, &c. & titul 25. de alend. libr. & part. Cur autem ille sit prior isto; ratio hæc est, tum quia ille prioribus titulis est similior, in eo, quod ut priores de divortio ad divortium aliqui pertinent ita & hoc divortio facto &c. tum quia prius, an & ubi sint educandi, quæri debet quæ à quo alantur. Præterea tit. posterior non tantum est de liberis, sed etiam de parentibus. Tractatus autem de parentibus ad matrimonium non pertinet, sed ad liberis, qui sunt fructus matrimonij, pertinet. Sic & infra ubi de tutel. prior est titul. ubi pupil. educar. &c. titulo de ipsis alendis liberis, puta tit. 49. tit. 50. infr. h. lib. 5. & ultimum partim est de concubinis, titul. 26. de concubinis, partim de liberis nat. turalibus, titul. 27. de lib. nat. Ratio inter hos 2. titul. est cur de concubinis sit prior, tum quia jus de concubinis est antiquum jus de naturalibus liberis est longè recentius, ab Imp. Constantino introductum Nov. 89. tum quia naturales liberi sunt illi, qui ex concubinis, vel ex ancillis nascuntur. Effectus autem causa sua posterior. Adhæc dictum est de actione dotis, quæ est prior pars hoc libr. 5. & nascitur ex æquo & bono, ut supra dic&tum. Huic nunc adjungitur actio tutelæ quæ est altera pars hujus libr ƒ. sed deinde x q. contractu est hoc est tutela sive potius administratione tutelæ. ƒ. tutor. Institut. de obligat. quæ ex q. contract. Ratio exponitur ad ff. ut autem in actione dotis de matrimonio & aliis ad dotem constituendam idoneis ita & hic de tutelis omnia diligenter explicantur. tit.ul. 48. ut supra dictum. Quorum ordo ut sit dilucidior, ad IX. capita erunt revocanda I. continet species tutelæ, de quo est titul.28. & 8. seqq. II. de administratione sive officio tutorum, de quo est tit.ul.37. & 13. seqq. III. est de ipsa act. tutelæ de qua est titul. 51. & 7. sequentib. IV. est de auctoritate tutor. titul. 59. V. est de finienda tutela. titul.60. & seq. VI. est de excusatione tutorum, titul.62. & 7. seqq. VII. est de curatore furiosi. titul.70. XVIII. est de prædiis minorum, titul.71. & 3. seq. IX. & ultim. est de magistratibus conveniendis, titul. 65. & ultim. hoc tit. In ff. quia ordo paulo est alius. ratio ejus erit utrobique explicanda. Et primum quidem de ordine 9. cap. inter se, cur species tutelæ primo exponantur. ratio dicta est supra ad Institut ubi & de secundo capite dictum ad titulum de auctoritate tutor. Tertij capitis, quod est de Actionibus hæc est ratio, quia actio est effectus administrationis, quæ est quasi contractus, unde hæc actio nascitur. De rel. quiis conjunctionibus capp. dicetur infra ad finum quoque caput. Quod ergo ad singulos titulos attinet, primo ponitur titul.28. de testament. tutel. Ratio in Institut exposita. Cui adjungitur titul. 19. de confirm. tutor. Ratio in ff. afferetur. Eum statim sequitur titul 30. de legit. tut. Est enim hæc secunda tutelæ species. Curitas dictum jam est in Institut. Hunc sequitur tertia quæ est dativa, ad quam pertinet titul.31. & 5. seqq. inter quos 4 titulos de tutela dativa, primus est titul.31. qui petant. tutor. Cur hic primo loco ponatur, hæc est ratio, quia prius tutor petatur quam detur. Ad petitionem quoque pertinet titul.32. ubi petantur tut. &c. Nam prius de eo, qui petat, & posterius de eo, coram quo vel ubi petitur. Reliquis 2. titulis agitur de ipsis tutoribus dativis, qui petuntur sive dantur. Et inter hos prior est titul 33. de tutor. vel curat. ailing. propter dignitatem personæ pupillaris: posterior est titul 34. qui uare tutor. &c. in quo non tantum de tutoribus, qui dantur, sed etiam de magistratu. qui dat, agitur, quæ etiam causa est cur hic posterior, quia 2. continet. Huic adjungitur titul.35. quandomulier, &c. Adhuc enim de tutore dictum quia tutela virile munus est, ex leg. 2. de reg. l. jur. sed hic adjungitur exceptio, quæ posterior est regula, quia interdum mater & avia tutelæ officio fungun-tur ex novis constitutionibus. Hunc sequitur tit.36. in quibus causis. Ratio est, quia priores tituli omnes sunt de primo, hic est de secundo tutore, & proinde posterior. ut supra dictum de rejiciunt. in integrum. titulum si sæpius in integr. Et hæc de primo cap. Proximum est caput de officio tutoris, quod in administratione ponitur. Eo igitur pertinet titul. 37. De administr. tut. qui est 1. in hoc capite, quia est generalis, cui adjungitur titulus 38. de peric. tut. Ratio est quia ex administratione, aut etiam interdum sine ea, tutori est periculum: adhæret scilicet periculum administrationi. Itaque in ff. utrumque sub eodem titulo côtinetur. Eum sequitur titulus 30. quando ex facto, &c. Nam hic titulus est velut species tituli prioris, qui est de omni periculo, hoc est, tantum de actione: & prior est tantum de tutoris periculo: hic est de pupilli periculo & commodo. Sic & titulus prox. 40. si ex plur. tut. &c. Continet speciem tit. de admin. ff. & tut. de peric. & c. Est enim de actione, sed ut prior titulus 39. de actione, quam pupillus exercet vel excipit nomine suo, ita hic titulus 40. est de ea actione, quam tutor exercet vel excipit nomine pupilli. Nam de actione, quæ contra tutorem à minore exercetur quæ est actio tutelæ, dicetur infra. Hoc actionis exercitium, sive pupilli defensio est pars administrationis. Huic titulo adjungitur titulus 41. Ne tut. vel curat. &c. qui tit. quia est prohibitorius, proinde est posterior. Prohibitio autem hæc ad administrationem pertinet, eâ scilicet de causa, ut tutor officii suî melius faciat, sic & titulus 42. de tut. & curat. qui fieri, &c. Est prohibitorius, quia tutor prohibetur prorsus administrare, qui non ante fatisdedit. Huic adjungitur tit. 43. de suspect. tut. & curat. Nam & hic est prohibitorius: imo tutor suspectus non tantum prohibetur ab administratione, ut vô fatisdans, verum etiam plane removetur, idque interdum cum infamia, quæ quia est pœna, idcirco hic titulus est posterior: quin etiam ratio inter hos titulos prohibitorios ex hac gradatione intelligitur, quod titul 41. prohibetur tutor non administrare sed alienatitulus 42. prohibetur etiam pupillaria, quod est gravius, titulus 43. prohibetur omnino, quod est gravissimum. Hunc titulum sequitur tit. 44. de in litem dando tutore &c. Ratio est quia ad ninistratio, vel est negotiorum, de qua hactenus dictum, vel est litium, de qua hic. Huic adjungitur titulus 45. de eo qui pro tut. &c. Ratio est perspicua, quia hactenus dictum de administratione veri tutoris, nunc de administratione falsi. Hunc sequitur titulus 46. si mater, &c. Ratio est, quia & hic titulus ad titulum de administratione pertinet, puta, si mater indemnitatem promisit, aut alii propinqui. Cui adjungitur titulus 47. si contra matris, &c. hic titulus tantum adjicitur propter mentionem matris jam factam de periculo administrationis. Nam alioqui hic titulus si contra matrem, &c. huc proprie non pertinet. Est enim potius de remotione, quam de administratione tutoris. Huc sequitur tit. 48. ut cause post pub. &c. hac ratione, quia hactenus dictum est de administratione, durante tutela, nunc de ea quæ est finita tutela, sive post pubertatem. Ultimum locum in hoc cap. de officio tutoris obtinet educatio, & alimentorum præstatio, de quibus duobus sunt titulus 49. ubi pupilli educ. & titulus 50. de alimentis pupillo præstand. Ratio ordinis, cur hæc pars officii de educando pupillo postremo loco ponatur, est, quia est tanquam species sive pars officii. Priores autem tituli sunt generales. Specialia sunt generalibus posteriora. Est & altera ratio, quia administratio negotiorum & litium semper tutoribus incumbat, educatio non semper, sed matri saepe, & aliis propinquis committitur. l.1. C.h.tit. Inter hos autem duo stit. Cur ille, ubi pupilli edu. &c. prior si altero de alimen. praest. ratio haec est, quia prius semper de loco ubi quid fiat, quam de re ipsa agitur, ut videre est in tit. de jud ubi quaeritur primum de judice competente, hoc est ubi sit litigandum, & ubi actiones instituendae. Posterius de ipsis actionibus agitur. Et haec hactenus de primo & secundo, huius tractatus de tutela, postea de ipso tutore & ejus officio, cujus & pars aliqua de auctor. tutor. huc pertinens, rejicitur tamen ad tit 59.infr. ubi ratio indicabitur. III. Caput de tutelis est de ipsa tutelae actione. Ratio supra expositia est. Est enim haec actio, velut effectus administrationis & proinde posterior, de qua actione est titul 51.arbitr.tutel. Hunc sequitur tit. 52.de divid. tut. Ratio ordinis est quia prior tit. est generalis de natura hujus actionis, hic est specialis, puta si plures sint tutores, an ea actione omnes teneantur. Eadem est ratio ordinis in ff. ad titul. de duol reus qui titulus subsequitur titulum generalem de verbor.obl. Ad hanc actionem tutelae pertinet tit. 53.de in lit.j n. Ratio, quia priores tituli sunt de hac actione sive ejus natura, cui, contra quem detur: hic jam est de ea exercenda, an scilicet in ea in litem juretur. Quaero, cur hic titul. ad actionem tutelae hic in Cod accommodetur, cum in litem jusjurandum etiam ad alias actiones pertineat. Ratio haec est quia in litem jusjurandum in actione tutelae maxime praestatur adversus heredes tutoris, leg.1.Cod.de inlit.jur. Ideo que titulus de hered.tut. qui est 54. hic adjungitur: nam postquam de ipso tutore, qui hac actione tutelae tenetur, actum est, proximum est de hisce ejus heredibus explicare. Itaque hi duo tituli 53. & 54. recte hic conjunguntur. Prior tamen est de in lit jurand. quia hoc jusjurandum, et si plerunque contra heredem, interdum tamen etiam contra ipsum tutorem praestatur, leg.2.C.hoc tit Huic titulo, ne heredib.tutor. jam adjungitur titul. 55.si tutor non geffer. Nam & hic pertinet ad actionem tutelae, sed quia prius agendum est de tutore, qui gessit, an teneatur hac actione, subsequitur recte de tutore, qui non gessit; nam & hic tenetur. His de actionibus titulis adjunguntur duo tituli accessorii, puta tit 56.de ufur.pr.p.& tit. 57.de fid.juss.tut.&c. Notum est, usuram & fidejussores jure dici accessiones. Accessoria autem principalibus sunt posteriora. Cur autem titulus de ufur. fit prior eo, qui est de fidejussor. Ratio haec est: quia ut priores tituli ad tutorem, sed de re principali, pupillorum: ita & hic quoque titulus ad tutorem pertinet, sed est de usuris. Ratio autem postulat, ut prius agatur de tutore, hoc est reo principali, quam de accessorio, sive tutoris fidejussore. Hunc titul. de fidejussor.tut. sequitur titul. 58. de contrariatutel. Prius scilicet de recto agendum fuit, posterius de contrario tutelae judicio, ut & in ff. ratio postulat. Et haec de tertio capite. IV. Est de auctoritate.
units.tr: Now let us turn to the sixth book. Its titles (there are sixty-two) can conveniently be reduced to the following heads. I. Concerns the action for theft. II. Concerns the action for services (operarum) and other matters pertaining to the rights of patrons and freedmen. III. Concerns possession of goods (bonorum possessio). IV. Concerns inheritance, both by testament and on intestacy. V. Is an accessory matter. Many do not grasp the order of these chapters and of the whole book. From the order of the Perpetual Edict it can be understood that the Edict of Tribonian follows the Code more than the Digest, as said before. The order of the Edict was therefore this (for the matter must be traced a little further back): first the civil actions were placed in the edict, then the praetorian ones, and the civil judicial actions came before the praetorian because they are more excellent, as also said elsewhere. Tribonian kept this order both in the Digest and in the Code, although he sometimes departs from it, as we have warned above. Of the actions we have so far set out, most are civil, except for a few praetorian ones which, on account of their similarity, were joined to the civil ones. Now reason requires that, having explained the civil actions, we pass to the praetorian. The beginning of these was in the edict with the action for theft, or certainly with possession of goods. The action for theft is in a way intermediate: partly civil, concerning theft not caught in the act, and partly praetorian, concerning theft caught in the act. §. sunt autem, Inst. de nox. act. But in pursuing these praetorian actions and in treating them in order, Tribonian often departs from the order of the Perpetual Edict and inserts many matters for particular reasons, which we shall explain in their place. From this it is already clear why in this book the action for theft is treated right at the beginning, in tit.2.de furtis & servo corrupt. The reason is that the action for theft is very similar to the action for rendering accounts (rationibus distrahendis), which pertains to guardianships, so much so that a guardian who sells off the property of his ward with intent to steal is liable not only to the action for rendering accounts but also to the charge of theft, l.1.§.pen.l.2.de tut.& ratio.distrah. That the action for theft stood in the Perpetual Edict immediately before the action for rendering accounts, and that civil actions were placed after the praetorian ones, as I said above of the first Edict, is plain from the books of Gaius and Paul on the Edict, and also from Paul, lib.2.sent.tit.30. & seq. But why the title de furtis comes before tit.de serv.fugitiv.&c., which is the first of this book, is explained thus: theft is for the most part committed by slaves. For the two common and linked faults of slaves are flight and theft, and flight comes first, because it teaches theft, which is, as Martial elegantly says, like a pupil of flight. For this reason, in the sale of slaves, it has long been customary to require a guarantee that the slave is neither a runaway nor a thief (l.1. de edil. edict., and likewise Cujacius in his Paratitla). But why subtic. 2. is joined with the corrupted slave is explained by the similarity of the subject: for both flight and theft are faults and corruptions of slaves, as has just been said. These are the things concerning the first chapter of this book, on the action for theft and the action concerning a corrupted slave, which two actions are separated by a long interval in the Digest. The second chapter concerns the action for services (operarum), on which is tit. 3. with the following titles.
